subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.

questions.q: In a transverse wave, how do the particles vibrate relative to the direction of energy transfer?
options: Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
At right angles to the direction of energy transfer
In a circular path around a fixed point
They do not vibrate at all
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction in which the wave transfers energy.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explain: Frequency is the number of waves passing a point each second, measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz. What does this tell you about its period?
options: The period cannot be found from frequency
questions.explain: Period T = 1/f = 1/50 = 0.02 s, since period and frequency are reciprocals.

questions.q: A wave travels at 340 m/s with a frequency of 170 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.explain: Using v = fλ, λ = v/f = 340/170 = 2.0 m.

questions.q: For waves travelling at a constant speed, how are frequency and wavelength related?
questions.explain: Since v = fλ is constant, increasing the frequency decreases the wavelength, so they are inversely proportional.

questions.q: Which feature is characteristic of a longitudinal wave?
questions.explain: Longitudinal waves consist of compressions and rarefactions as particles vibrate parallel to the direction of travel.

questions.q: According to the law of reflection, how does the angle of incidence compare with the angle of reflection?
options: The angle of incidence is greater
The angle of reflection is greater
questions.explain: For reflection at a plane surface, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.

questions.q: A ray of light passes from air into a glass block. How does it bend?
options: Towards the normal, because it slows down
Away from the normal, because it slows down
Towards the normal, because it speeds up
It does not bend at all
questions.explain: Light slows when entering the optically denser glass, so it refracts towards the normal.

questions.q: Which equation defines the refractive index n for light passing from air into a medium?
questions.explain: The refractive index is defined as n = sin i / sin r, where i and r are the angles of incidence and refraction.

questions.q: A ray enters a medium where sin i = 0.80 and sin r = 0.50. What is the refractive index?
Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from glass into air only if the angle of incidence is:
questions.explain: Total internal reflection happens when light in the denser medium meets the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle.

questions.q: A glass has a refractive index of 1.5. What is its critical angle (sin c = 1/n)?
Which type of lens is a converging lens?
questions.explain: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges (brings together) parallel rays to a focus.

questions.q: Which statement about a real image formed by a converging lens is correct?
options: It can be projected onto a screen
It is always the same size as the object
It cannot be formed by a lens
questions.explain: A real image is formed where light rays actually meet, so it can be captured on a screen.

questions.q: Which sequence lists the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency?
options: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma
Gamma, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Visible, radio, gamma, infrared, microwave, X-rays, ultraviolet
Infrared, radio, visible, gamma, microwave, ultraviolet, X-rays
questions.explain: Frequency increases from radio waves through to gamma rays across the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: At what speed do all electromagnetic waves travel in a vacuum?
questions.explain: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed of approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.

questions.q: Which type of electromagnetic radiation has the highest frequency and shortest wavelength?
questions.explain: Gamma rays lie at the high-frequency, short-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: Which everyday application uses infrared radiation?
options: Sterilising surgical instruments with gamma rays
questions.explain: Warm objects emit infrared, so thermal imaging cameras detect infrared radiation to show temperature.

questions.q: Which statement about sound waves is correct?
options: They are longitudinal and need a medium to travel
They are transverse and can travel through a vacuum
They are longitudinal and can travel through a vacuum
They are transverse and need a medium to travel
questions.explain: Sound is a longitudinal wave that requires particles of a medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.q: If the frequency of a sound wave is increased, how does the sound change?
questions.explain: The pitch of a sound is determined by its frequency, so higher frequency gives a higher pitch.
